title: The Last Wolf Anew
premise: Orsen Whitlock, a royal food-taster who secretly sells outlawed charms to survive, discovers that the child at his door is the last living vessel of an ancient covenant between the human realm and the wolf-spirits who once guarded its borders. Hunted by Chancellor Veyra—who has been draining the covenant's power to fuel her own immortality—Orsen and the child flee across a kingdom whose memories of magic are being erased one district at a time. To reforge the covenant, Orsen must surrender his own accumulated immunity, which has unknowingly made him a living archive of every poison and spell he has tasted. In the end, he gives up his memories of the child to complete the rite, saving both realms but forgetting why the small wolf-eyed figure watching him from across the market feels so heartbreakingly familiar.
about_author: August Oyelaran is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing oral histories from border villages before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about ordinary people caught in the machinery of old bargains.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. We meet him mid-service at the palace, detecting henbane in a stew meant for the king, then slipping home to sell a luck-charm to a laundress in defiance of the Edict of Ash. The emotional beat is quiet double-life tension: competence masking fear.

chapters.title: A Door That Should Not Open
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A child appears at his door speaking Old Covenant tongue—a language only found in sealed archives—and carrying a wolf-tooth sigil that burns Orsen's charm-work cold. He realizes someone marked his shop. The beat: dread blooming into reluctant responsibility.

chapters.title: The Chancellor's Kindness
chapters.summary: Veyra's POV. The Chancellor interrogates Orsen with unsettling warmth, revealing she knows about his charms but offers protection—for a price: the child. Flashbacks hint Veyra once served the old covenant faithfully. The beat: seductive menace.

chapters.title: Running on Empty Streets
chapters.summary: Orsen and the child, Wren, flee through districts where street names literally change overnight as memory-erasure spreads. An old fence sacrifices herself to buy them time. Beat: grief sharpening into resolve; trust between Orsen and Wren begins.

chapters.title: What the Wolves Remember
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, first time. In the ruins of a shrine, Wren shows Orsen visions of the original covenant—and of a human taster who betrayed it long ago. Orsen recognizes his own face. Beat: vertigo of inherited guilt.

chapters.title: The Price of Immunity
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A healer reveals his three years of tasting have made him a living archive—the only vessel that can hold the reforged covenant. But the rite will consume what he values most. Veyra's hunters close in. Beat: the terrible clarity of choice.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Ford
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Cornered at the river, Orsen accepts Veyra's bargain to save Wren from immediate death, handing over the sigil while secretly planning treachery. Wren witnesses the handover and their trust shatters. Beat: loyalty vs. truth made flesh.

chapters.title: The Hollow Court
chapters.summary: Veyra's POV. At the palace, Veyra begins the stolen rite and we learn her full history: she was the last covenant-keeper, corrupted by centuries of holding power alone. Orsen, imprisoned, tastes his way through her wards. Beat: villain rendered tragic; ticking clock accelerates.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POVs. Wren breaks Orsen out; together they interrupt the rite. Orsen drinks the concentrated covenant—every memory of Wren offered as fuel—and speaks the Old Tongue words Wren taught him. Veyra dissolves into the restored bond rather than let go of her power. Beat: sacrifice as triumph.

chapters.title: Small Charms
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Orsen's POV. Months later, magic is legal again and Orsen runs a modest charm-shop, immune to poison still but hollow in ways he can't name. A wolf-eyed child buys a luck-charm and lingers. Beat: bittersweet hope—the story ends on the edge of remembering.
